business_summary.text: KFin Technologies is a registrar and transfer agent and fund-accounting services provider to mutual funds, alternative investment funds, corporate issuers and pension schemes in India and internationally.

call_points.text: FY27 EBITDA growth guided at 17-20% and PAT growth at 12-15%, better than earlier forecast.
EBITDA margin 34.2% including Ascent versus 39.4% excluding it; cost savings visible from Q2.
About ₹40 crore of deals signed last quarter, to be recognised over 3 to 15 months.
Six new fund manager mandates above US$100 million won at Ascent, transitions from incumbents.
Cash of ₹687 crore at end-June; about ₹200 crore to go towards the declared dividend.
Corporate actions, about 30% of issuer solutions revenue, may stay tepid in Q2 on IT services dividend cuts.
Philippines pension contract not awarded; company was reported highest bidder, still in discussions.
Organic growth guided at ~15% with PAT growth a little over 11%, excluding Ascent.
International revenue guided to grow over 70% in FY27, including Ascent; organic international revenue over 60%.
Ascent won 5 new fund contracts with over $100 million AUM; one started in March, three start later this quarter, the rest in Q2.
Issuer Solutions crossed 10,500 corporate clients and targets ~11,500 in FY27; market share expanded ~80 bps QoQ.
A proposed single point-of-sale KYC ID could remove a meaningful part of KRA revenue from fetch costs, though not yet operational.
A ₹12.6 Cr one-time Labour Code impact hit FY26 and will not recur from FY27.

guidance.statement: FY27 revenue growth projected at 23-24% on a consolidated basis, described as an internal projection rather than formal guidance.
FY27 PAT growth projected at around 10%.
Organic revenue growth (excluding Ascent) guided at close to 15% with PAT growth a little over 11%.
International revenue guided to grow over 70% in FY27 including Ascent; organic international revenue over 60%.
EBITDA margin in the range of 40-45%, maintaining 40% threshold including Ascent by end of this year
Ascent to reach double-digit EBITDA margin within the next 12 months
International business to continue growing over 25%

industry: Financial Services > Capital Markets > Depositories, Clearing Houses and Other Intermediaries

operating_notes.text: Domestic mutual fund revenue share was 61% in Q4FY26; management aims to bring it below 50% over five years.
Ascent's Q4FY26 EBITDA margin was 8% and its yield is 6-7 bps.
KFin won 4 new AMC mandates in FY26 and services 4 of the top 10 fastest-growing AMCs by AUM.
Mutual fund fee-based revenue fell to 55% of total revenue in Q1FY27 from about 66% in Q1FY26, while non-MF revenue rose to 38% from 24.5%.
Ascent revenue rose to US$5.9 million in Q1FY27 from US$5.7 million in Q4 and US$4.4 million in Q1FY26, a 32% YoY increase.
Corporate actions are about 30% of issuer solutions revenue; KFin managed about 80% by market cap of main board IPOs in Q1 and holds 50% share of NSE 500 companies.

timeline.summary: KFin's Q4 FY26 earnings call (April 30, 2026) guided FY27 revenue growth at 23-24%, EBITDA 16-17% and PAT ~10%, with FY26 revenue up 19.3% and core PAT at ₹353 Cr.

watchlist.response: Management said the 23-24% revenue projection is not formal guidance and it still aims to cross 40% EBITDA margin in FY27.
watchlist.text: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of ~39% is below the earlier 40%+ target after Ascent integration.

watchlist.response: Management said Ascent was always around 7 bps and the variation is due to asset mix, particularly crypto funds.
watchlist.text: Ascent's yield has fallen from 8-9 bps to 6-6.5 bps.

watchlist.response: Management attributed the drop to mark-to-market losses and delayed deal closures, expecting some to fructify in the current quarter.
watchlist.text: Alternatives, private wealth and PMS revenue fell to ₹16 Cr in Q4FY26 from ₹20.7 Cr in Q3FY26.

watchlist.response: Management asked the analyst to connect with the IR team for segmental profitability details, without giving figures on the call
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for segment-wise profitability of mutual fund, issuer solutions and others

watchlist.response: Management said about 30% of the 2% impact was from debt-to-liquid movement, with the rest largely provisions for a pending renewal, partly offset by ETF-to-equity movement
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the split of the 2% yield decline between debt-to-liquid mix and contract renegotiation provisions

watchlist.response: Management declined to guide, saying 50-60% of yield depends on asset class and AMC growth outside its control
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for a yield guidance for the remaining three quarters
